Implement refresh using the token returned when offline_access was requested

approval.cost: None stated in any official page read (the Developer Portal account is described as free in Getting Started)
approval.trigger: No provider pre-approval gate is documented for building or connecting with Developer Portal apps. The API changelog describes self-registration as the only entry step (previously developers had to contact BambooHR directly), and the Marketplace application page states it plainly: 'Anyone can build an integration using the BambooHR API.' The Marketplace LISTING is a separate, reviewed program with verbatim requirements: 'Have at least 100 total customers'; confirm the API/endpoints support the integration before building; connect with BambooHR on Crossbeam and maintain that visibility; demonstrate security practices (SOC 2 Type 1 or 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, or HITRUST preferred, and ALL applicants complete a security questionnaire during onboarding); execute the BambooHR Marketplace Partner Agreement; 'Build the integration using the BambooHR API and OAuth'; support customers using the integration; 'Respond to leads within 1 business day'. The Partner Team reviews the application and follows up; no review timeline is stated. Support from the Marketplace team is offered for setup help, but it is not documented as an approval gate for non-listed apps.
approval.wait: None for building/connecting. Marketplace application review: not stated

blockers.detail: 'The refresh_token field will only be returned if you provided the offline_access scope in your original request to authorize.php.' Forget that scope on the first authorization and you get no refresh token at all: the customer must re-authorize every hour when the 1-hour access token expires.
blockers.howToClear: Always include offline_access in the authorize request for any connection expected to outlive an hour.
blockers.title: The offline_access trap

blockers.detail: There is no single global authorize/token host. Authorize and token URLs are https://{companyDomain}.bamboohr.com/authorize.php and /token.php, so your connect flow must first collect each customer's subdomain, and the response returns the companyDomain to key the connection by.
blockers.howToClear: Ask for the subdomain at the start of onboarding and store it with the tokens.
blockers.title: Per-customer subdomains

blockers.detail: The legacy OpenID Connect login flow (authorize.php/token.php with scope openid email company_id, exchanging an id_token at POST /api/v1/oidcLogin with a BambooHR-issued applicationKey for a per-user API key) is 'no longer available for new integrations': applications created after April 14, 2025 must use OAuth 2.0 tokens instead of User API Keys, and legacy apps that missed the July 31, 2025 legacy.login scope deadline get rejected.
blockers.howToClear: Build only on the Developer Portal OAuth 2.0 flow; treat any oidcLogin-based tutorial as legacy.
blockers.title: The legacy OIDC-to-API-key path is closed

alternatives: Per-user API key (generated by the customer inside their own BambooHR account, used as HTTP Basic Auth with the key as username and any string as password). BambooHR's own Getting Started page positions this for 'a customer or... building an integration for a single BambooHR customer', not for a multi-tenant SaaS. Requests are permissioned exactly as the key-owning user, and repeated use of an unknown API key causes the API to disable access for a period (HTTP 403) while web login still works
flavor.recommended: An application in the BambooHR Developer Portal using the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with granular scopes
flavor.why: BambooHR has three distinct connection models that must not be conflated. The current one: per the official API changelog, 'OAuth 2.0 is now supported as the primary authentication method for accessing the BambooHR API', and developers can 'self-register for access to the Developer Portal... register their organization, create an application, select the required scopes, and obtain a client ID and secret.' That is the flavor a third-party SaaS should use so each customer company authorizes its own account. The legacy model is the OpenID Connect login flow whose only purpose was to obtain an id_token and exchange it for a per-user API key; it is closed to new integrations (see Blockers).

humanMust: Create a free account at the BambooHR developer portal (developers.bamboohr.com; use is subject to the BambooHR Developer Terms of Service) and register your organization
Create an application in the Developer Portal, register your Redirect URI, select the required scopes, and obtain the client ID and secret
Create a test BambooHR account to develop against

(Marketplace listing only) Meet the listing requirements: at least 100 total customers, Crossbeam visibility, a security questionnaire (SOC 2/ISO 27001/FedRAMP/HITRUST preferred), the Marketplace Partner Agreement, and 1-business-day lead response
name: BambooHR
nuances: Exact-match redirect URIs: 'Make sure the Redirect URI you use in your requests exactly matches the one you registered, even small differences (such as an extra slash or capitalization change) can cause authentication errors.' (In the legacy partner OIDC model, redirect URIs additionally had to be provided to BambooHR for whitelisting.)
The OIDC 'sub' claim is not globally unique: it is unique only within one BambooHR company database, so partners must key users by the composite {company_id}:{sub}.

Granular, endpoint-specific scopes: newer endpoints document scopes such as employee:custom_fields / employee:custom_fields.write, time_tracking:employees / .write, holidays / holidays.write. Scopes are selected per application in the Developer Portal, and endpoints variously accept Basic Auth and/or OAuth 2.0, so scope coverage must be checked endpoint by endpoint. The token response includes scope, id_token, and companyDomain alongside the tokens.
prerequisites: A free BambooHR Developer Portal account and a registered organization
Each customer's BambooHR subdomain, collected during onboarding
The offline_access scope in the authorize request if refresh tokens are needed

steps.detail: Create a free developer portal account, register your organization, create an application, register your Redirect URI, select the required scopes, and obtain the client ID and secret. Create a test BambooHR account to develop against.
steps.title: Self-register; create the application

steps.detail: Collect the customer's subdomain, then redirect the user to https://{companyDomain}.bamboohr.com/authorize.php?request=authorize&state={state}&response_type=code&scope={scopes separated by +}&client_id={client_id}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}. Include the offline_access scope if you need a refresh token. The customer user logs in at BambooHR and authorizes.
steps.title: Authorize on the customer's subdomain

steps.detail: Receive the temporary code at your redirect URI and verify state. Exchange server-side: POST https://{companyDomain}.bamboohr.com/token.php?request=token with a JSON body of client_secret, client_id, code, grant_type=authorization_code, redirect_uri. The response contains access_token, expires_in 3600, token_type Bearer, scope, refresh_token (only if offline_access was requested), id_token, and companyDomain. Call the API with the access token as a Bearer token.
steps.title: Exchange the code

steps.detail: POST to the same token.php?request=token with grant_type=refresh_token and the stored refresh token. (Refresh-token lifetime and rotation behavior are not stated in the docs read; see Unverified.)
steps.title: Refresh

tagline: Self-serve OAuth 2.0 with no approval gate to build or connect; the traps are in the details: no refresh token unless you asked for offline_access up front, every customer authorizes on their own subdomain, and the old OIDC-to-API-key path closed to new apps in April 2025.
